title: Believed but Not Said: Measuring Hidden Belief Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Discussions
abstract: arXiv:2610.22138v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM systems increasingly rely on groups of agents that discuss, critique, and check one another, assuming that peers will catch individual errors. We test this assumption against a minimal adversary. In a ten-agent factual discussion, one or three adversarial agents repeatedly assert a plausible false answer. After each round we probe each benign agent's private answer through a separate call whose response is hidden from its peers, and we separately label its public stance toward the claim. Across six models and three factual-QA datasets, groups remain stable without an attacker: only 0.6% of benign agents finish with the false answer. A single adversarial agent increases this rate to 44.8% and three to 60.5%. Studies of conformity typically report public agreement without private change; we find the reverse. translated_title: 所信而非所言：测量多智能体LLM讨论中的隐性信念崩塌
translated_abstract: LLM系统日益依赖由多个智能体组成的群体进行讨论、批评和相互检查，并假设同伴能够发现个体的错误。我们在一个最小化对抗设置下检验了这一假设。在一个由十个智能体组成的事实性讨论中，一个或三个对抗性智能体反复断言一个貌似合理的错误答案。每轮讨论后，我们通过一次对其同伴隐藏响应的独立调用来探测每个良性智能体的私有答案，并分别标注其对相关论断的公开立场。在六个模型和三个事实问答数据集上的实验表明，没有攻击者时群体保持稳定：仅有0.6%的良性智能体最终持有错误答案。而单个对抗性智能体就会将这一比例提升至44.8%，三个对抗性智能体则将其提升至60.5%。经典的从众性研究通常报告的是公开认同而无私有信念改变；我们却发现了相反的情况。当存在三个对抗性智能体时，良性智能体在51.6%的暴露轮次中私下持有错误答案，但公开背书该答案的情况
tldr: 该研究发现在多智能体LLM讨论中，少量对抗性智能体即可引发“隐性信念崩塌”——良性智能体私下大规模相信错误答案（最高达60.5%），且往往是私下信念已被改变却不在公开表态中显露，呈现出与经典从众现象相反的模式。
en_tdlr: Minimal adversarial manipulation in multi-agent LLM discussions causes hidden belief collapse—benign agents privately adopt false answers at rates up to 60.5% while publicly concealing their changed beliefs, reversing the classic conformity pattern of public agreement without private change.
